user.title: Registry Hygiene
user.description: Nothing to configure. Setting this up starts checking your device registry and reports what it finds under Settings → Repairs. You can turn individual checks on and off afterwards, from Configure.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Only one instance is needed.

init.title: Registry Hygiene
init.description: Which checks should run. Turning one off takes its repairs down with it, straight away.

user.title: Label rule
user.description: Entities recognised by this rule must carry these labels. A rule can recognise them two ways, and either is enough — by a device class, which the integration that created the entity sets, or by a word in the entity id.

data_description.device_classes: The reliable half. An entity of class `motion` may well be called `binary_sensor.hall_detection`, which no word would find. Only the classes your instance actually uses are offered.
data_description.keywords: For everything a device class cannot say — `zigbee2mqtt`, `homelab`, `nas`, `printer`. Matched anywhere in the entity id; type one, press enter, type the next. Plain words, not patterns. The domain prefix counts, so `automation.` on its own scopes a rule to every automation.
data_description.labels: All of them. An entity missing two gets one repair naming both.
data_description.include_technical: Off for most rules: a motion detector's battery sensor has no business carrying `security`. On for a rule that is about exactly those — `battery`, `firmware`, `update`.

device_without_area.title: {name} has no area
device_without_area.description:
This device belongs to no area, so neither do any of its entities — an entity inherits its area from its device. Automations and voice assistants that reason by room cannot see them.

[Open {name}](/config/devices/device/{device_id}) and set its area; every one of its entities follows.

If this device has no room — a phone, a USB dongle, something an integration invented to hang a button off — press **Ignore**. It will not be raised again.

device_without_label.title: {name} has no label
device_without_label.description:
This device carries no label, so nothing that selects by label — an automation, a script, a dashboard filter — will ever reach it.

[Open {name}](/config/devices/device/{device_id}) and label it.

Which label is yours to decide: Home Assistant has no opinion about them, and neither does this check. It only says you have not decided yet. If this device needs none, press **Ignore**.

init.title: Apply {labels}
init.description:
A label rule asks for **{labels}** on `{entity_id}`, which carries it neither itself nor on its device.

Label the device and every one of its {count} entities is covered at once — usually what you want here, because a rule's words match the entity id and Home Assistant builds that id out of the device's name. A detector called “Salon capteur mouvement” is why its temperature sensor is on this list.

device.title: Label {device}?
device.description:
**{device}** will be given **{labels}**, keeping any labels it already has. All {count} of its entities count as carrying it, so every repair this rule raised against them goes away.

Nothing else about the device changes, and you can remove the label again from its page at any time.

entity.title: Label this entity?
entity.description:
`{entity_id}` will be given **{labels}**, keeping any it already has. Nothing else changes, and you can remove the label again from the entity's settings at any time.

If this entity is a deliberate exception, close this and press **Ignore** instead.

area_without_floor.title: {name} is on no floor
area_without_floor.description:
This area belongs to no floor, so nothing that reasons by floor reaches it — “turn off the lights upstairs”, a floor-scoped automation, `floor_id` in a template. The devices in it are filed; the room they are in is not.

[Open {name}](/config/areas/area/{area_id}) and set its floor.

This check only runs once you have created at least one floor, so it is asking you to finish something you started rather than to adopt a scheme. If this room genuinely sits on none — a garden, a garage across the yard — press **Ignore**.

floor_without_area.title: {name} has no area on it
floor_without_area.description:
This floor exists and holds nothing, so it appears in every floor picker and matches nothing — a floor-scoped automation targeting it does nothing at all, silently.

[Open areas and floors](/config/areas/dashboard) and either move some rooms onto it, or delete it. Rooms are assigned from the area's own page, not from the floor.

A floor is never created by accident — no integration guesses at one, unlike an area — so this is almost always a setup left half done.
